Then, there's a lot going on with the disks. Both sda and sdb on various nodes show very high read/write rates, especially for MG02 and Mysql02. Also, the MySQL-related metrics like Innodb data pending fsyncs and threads running are elevated, suggesting possible database contention or slow writes.

Looking at the logs, there are several GC errors in Tomcat instances. This indicates memory pressure, maybe due to high request volumes leading to frequent garbage collection pauses. If the application servers (Tomcats) are under memory stress, they might not handle requests efficiently, leading to higher CPU usage and disk I/O as the system tries to compensate.

The propagation shows that IG01 and IG02 are upstream to all Tomcats, so if those are problematic, they could be causing the downstream issues. Also, the network metrics show high TCP FIN-WAIT states, which could mean connection leaks or improper closure, leading to resource exhaustion. This would affect the ability of the system to handle new connections, contributing to the overall load on the servers.

Considering the component graph, Tomcat instances depend on MG (which includes MG01 and MG02) and Redis. So if the databases (Mysql01/02, Redis02) are under strain, that could impact the Tomcats. But the highest peaks in the metrics are in the disk and CPU areas, particularly for MG02 and Mysql02. 

Putting this together, the top three components would likely be the ones with the most direct impact. The high CPU on IG02, the disk I/O on MG02 and Mysql02, and the memory issues in Tomcat instances. These factors interconnect, but the immediate root causes would be the CPU overuse, disk saturation, and memory pressure leading to GC issues.
